$comment: The same OpenVINO IR model run on three devices in one machine, in one process, back to back. The CPU and the integrated GPU are indistinguishable here -- their 95% intervals overlap almost entirely -- and routing the same model to the discrete NVIDIA GPU through OpenVINO is about four times slower while drawing nearly twice the power. That last figure is a statement about OpenVINO's generic GPU path, NOT about the card: llama.cpp reaches this GPU through CUDA and is far faster on it. Absolute throughput here is not publishable -- background CPU was above this project's 20% threshold for part of the run -- but the discrete-GPU gap is an order of magnitude outside that noise, and the determinism finding does not depend on timing at all.

system.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Laptop GPU

gpus.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Laptop GPU

protocol.prompt: Explain what a token is in large language models, in two sentences.
protocol.order: cpu, GPU.0, GPU.1 -- consecutive, one process, no reload between devices

devices.vram_note: the run used Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (iGPU) but telemetry samples NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Laptop GPU; that device's memory and utilisation say nothing about this run, and an Intel iGPU allocates from shared system RAM where nvidia-smi cannot see it

devices.device_name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Laptop GPU (dGPU)

findings.claim: The CPU and the integrated GPU are indistinguishable for this model.
findings.evidence: 74.98 tok/s CI95 [71.27, 78.68] on the CPU against 75.97 tok/s CI95 [68.94, 83.0] on the iGPU; the intervals overlap across almost their whole width.
findings.not_concluded: That one is faster than the other. An earlier pass of this same sweep, taken while two unrelated test suites were running, appeared to show the CPU ahead by 15%. It was noise.

findings.claim: Greedy decoding is not reproducible on the Intel iGPU, and is on the CPU.
findings.evidence: Six greedy generations from the same prompt: 1 distinct output on the CPU, 4 distinct outputs on GPU.0.
findings.why_it_matters: Greedy decoding picks the highest-probability token, so it is deterministic by definition. Different outputs mean the device's kernels are producing slightly different logits run to run -- parallel reductions need not sum in the same order -- and near-ties flip the argmax. Any quality comparison that assumes a fixed seed and greedy decoding gives one answer is wrong on this device, and nothing in the run reports it.

findings.claim: Reaching the discrete GPU through OpenVINO is roughly four times slower than the CPU and draws nearly twice the power.
findings.evidence: 19.64 tok/s at 50.16 W, against 74.98 tok/s at 28.76 W on the CPU. Time to first token 332.23 ms against 62.03 ms.
findings.not_concluded: That this GPU is slow at inference. OpenVINO reaches it through a generic path rather than CUDA. For scale: this repository's own published llama.cpp CUDA result on the same card is 360.87 tok/s (results/published, qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf). That is a different model build and a different quantization, so it is NOT a like-for-like comparison and is quoted only to show the gap is far larger than a quantization difference explains.

findings.claim: Memory use on the integrated GPU was not measured.
findings.evidence: the run used Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (iGPU) but telemetry samples NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Laptop GPU; that device's memory and utilisation say nothing about this run, and an Intel iGPU allocates from shared system RAM where nvidia-smi cannot see it
findings.why_it_matters: Reported as absent rather than as 0.0. The figure nvidia-smi returns belongs to an idle discrete card, and publishing it against an iGPU run would say this model needs no memory.

caveats: Background CPU ranged from 5% to 28% across the three runs, against this project's 20% publish threshold. These are not published results and do not enter the dataset.
One model, one size (0.5B), one quantization (int4_asym, group 128). A larger model changes the memory picture and may change the ordering.
The NPU was not tested: the reference machine has none.
